column7: 2026-11-06: Retry-After feature (not started; user wants to review 429 dashboards first, do not implement until they say so). DECIDED by user: the wait is Retry-After PLUS the normal backoff delay (sum), not a replacement and not max(). Reason: billing's Retry-After is the moment their rate window reopens, and ~40 pods returning at exactly that moment get 429'd again; backoff on top spreads them out. Billing client already sets error.retryAfter in seconds. Design leaning (mine, not confirmed): generic hook option such as calculateDelay(context) returning ms, not built-in reading of error.retryAfter. Still OPEN, ask user: whether maxTimeout caps the Retry-After part, whether to fail fast when the wait exceeds remaining maxRetryTime, whether the wait applies when shouldConsumeRetry returns false, validation of NaN/negative/Infinity.

2026-11-06: Retry-After implemented (built into index.js, reads error.retryAfter seconds; not a generic hook, since user asked for built-in reading). Wait = retryAfter + backoff. My choices for the open points: maxTimeout caps only the backoff; wait is clamped by remaining maxRetryTime like any delay (no fail-fast); a non-consumed retry still waits retryAfter but no backoff; NaN/negative/0/Infinity/non-number retryAfter ignored, capped at setTimeout max. Tests in test-timing.js. Revisit if user wants fail-fast.
